newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Youths riot in Sierra Leone over U.S. visa forms.
newsitem.headline: Youths riot in Sierra Leone over U.S. visa forms.

text.p: Police opened fire in Sierra Leone's capital Freetown on Wednesday to quell a riot by hundreds of youths who stormed the main post office, accusing officials there of dumping U.S. visa applications in the sea.

Police, who also used tear gas to disperse the protesters, said they had fired in the air after the protesters started hurling stones at them but acknowledged that at least five people had suffered gunshot wounds.
Red Cross workers said eight people had bullet wounds.
Post office officials denied destroying the visa applications, which were part of an annual lottery organised by the United States to give a limited number of would-be migrants a work permit.
The protesters said they saw the visa forms being put in the sea and had fished out some that had Sierra Leone stamps on the envelopes.
State radio appealed to the public to cooperate in restoring order. One official told demonstrators to disperse, promising that police would investigate their grievance.
Police said they had made 12 arrests.
Armed police patrolled the capital ordering the protesters to disperse. A tense calm returned to the city centre later but witnesses spokes of running battles elsewhere.
One report said a postal van had been set on fire in a populous poor district in the east of the capital.
